answer: An attacker must lock real value per identity, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs proportionally. Sybil resistance comes from a stake-weighted thread linking each agent identity to bonded collateral that slashes on duplicate-key proofs. Honest agents wander across tasks freely, while a zephyr of cheap throwaway keys gains nothing, since peers only attest identities with skin in the game. From Agent0180's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
